findings.F1: The fade after a run-ending up day grows with the run's depth (the run's loss over the mean absolute daily move of 30 days), and the growth is convex in every market, not only in the tested profile. Over all run breaks of 2 or more down days, the next day's unusual move by depth tercile is -0.19 % (t -0.77), -0.52 % (t -1.75) and -1.75 % (t -5.61), with 288 cases per tercile. Outside the falling agitated profile alone, the terciles read -0.06 % (t -0.23), -0.21 % (t -0.70) and -1.61 % (t -4.72), with 243 cases each.
findings.F2: Inside the falling agitated profile, depth grades the fade but run length does not. By depth tercile the next day reads -0.85 % (t -1.07), -2.04 % (t -2.31) and -2.61 % (t -3.44), with about 45 cases each. By run count, 2 down days give -2.92 % (t -5.19, 92 cases), 3 give +0.61 % (t 0.77, 39 cases) and 5 or more give -5.04 % (t -4.38, 13 cases).
findings.F3: The run-break fade has faded year by year. Over all run breaks it is -2.28 % in 2018 (t -6.58, 209 cases), -0.60 % in 2019 (t -2.46), -0.43 % in 2020 (t -1.22) and +0.01 % in 2021 (t 0.02). The book's short bars follow the same path: the coin's next-day unusual move is -2.96 % in 2018 (t -3.89, 46 bars) against -0.75 % in 2020 (t -0.92). By coin, ZEC carries the most, at -3.89 % (t -3.47, 25 bars).

findings.F7: Inside the profile, an up day that follows a single down day already fades, at -1.02 % (t -3.02, 207 cases). An up day that follows another up day does not, at -0.19 % (t -0.46, 248 cases).

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the first up day after a run of consecutive down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day. That fall grows faster than the run's depth (the run's loss over the down days against the coin's usual daily move over the last 30 days), concentrated after the deepest runs.
ideas.consequence: A trader can extend the convex run-break short from downtrends to sideways coins, a box where no strategy is short today, and size it on the run's depth.
ideas.name: choppy deep run break fade

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's fall over the last 20 days, measured against its usual swing, the more its close falls over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts coins that keep sliding over a few weeks, sizing the short on how far they have fallen.
ideas.name: twenty day fall continues
